question: According to Sangam texts, the term uzhavar means:
solution:
The correct answer is **__ordinary ploughmen__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ordinary ploughmen** were known as **Uzhavar**.
 
• These were **individuals engaged in plowing and cultivating the land,** playing a vital role in the agrarian economy of the Sangam period.
 
• **Agriculture was a primary occupation **during this time, and Uzhavars were highly regarded in society for their contributions to food production and sustenance.
 
• **Landless labourers**, including **slaves**, were known as **Kadaisiyar and Adimai**.
 
• According to the early Tamil Literature (Sangam Texts), the large landowners living in the villages are called Vellalar__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• In the **northern part **of the country, the village **headman **was known as the **Gramabhojaka**.

 
 
• Usually, men from the same family held the position for generations.
 
• In other words, the **post **was **hereditary**.
 
• The **Gramabhojaka** was often the **largest landowner**. 
 
• He also **functioned **as a **judge**, and sometimes as a **policeman**.
 
• There were other independent farmers, known as **Grihapatis**, most of whom were **smaller landowners**.
 
• And then there were men and women such as the **Dasa Karmakara**, who did **not own land** and had to earn a living working on the fields owned by others.
